Scribble RelayProject record · built 2026-09-18 from main

Scribble Relay

A pass-the-device drawing party game for 3–12 players, played in the browser on one phone, tablet or laptop. One player writes a secret phrase, the next draws it, the next guesses the drawing, and so on. At the end the whole chain is revealed one step at a time so everyone sees how the message fell apart. Suggested by Claude on 2026-09-13 when Luqman asked for a party game idea; he picked it and asked for it to be built right away.

Main stackindex.html: HTML + CSS + JavaScript, Canvas 2D for the drawing pad. Since 2026-09-18 (merged to main as 12c62e2, live) a Phaser 4.2.1 effects layer (fx.js, vendored) draws confetti, stars and flashes over the page and plays Kenney CC0 sounds — the game itself stays HTML (D-004)

Why this project exists

Luqman wanted a party game that runs from a single HTML file. The pass-the-device format needs no server, no accounts and no phones joining a room, which is what makes one file enough. It also suits a Todak Academy class: drawing plus a game.

What counts as "done"

  1. A full chain plays end to end: write → draw → guess … → reveal.
  2. Each player only ever sees the turn directly before theirs.
  3. Comfortable on phone (portrait and landscape), tablet and desktop, with finger, stylus or mouse.
  4. The chain can be saved as one image to share.

All four hold as of 2026-09-13 (120/120 browser checks), but none has been tried at a real party yet.

What is NOT in scope

  • Online multiplayer or phones-as-controllers (needs a server — breaks the one-file idea)
  • Accounts, scoring leaderboards, saved game history

How the game gets made

Pipeline

Scribble Relay was pitched, built, tested and published in one session on 2026-09-13. It is one HTML file with no libraries and no server, tested by playing a whole game in headless Chrome and reading the screenshots. The one step still to come is a real party.

  1. IdeaClaude pitched three party games; Luqman picked drawing telephone on one shared device.01-idea.md
  2. DecidePass one device instead of phones joining a room, a public repo on GitHub Pages, and a fixed square canvas.06-decisions.md
  3. BuildThe whole game in one file: screens, the chain of turns, the drawing pad, sound made in code.index.html
  4. TestA full 4-player game in headless Chrome at phone, phone-landscape, tablet and desktop sizes, drawing with real touch and mouse input.test/run.sh, test/e2e.js
  5. LookEvery screen at every size is screenshotted and read by eye. This caught a hidden message peeking 1px above the bottom edge that the checks missed.test/shots/
  6. ShipPush to main and GitHub Pages rebuilds the live game within a minute.github.com/juslangit/scribble-relay
  7. PlaytestPlay with real people on a real phone and tablet, and write down what confuses them. Not done yet.03-milestones.md (M2)
  8. LogWhat was done, decided and learned in each session goes into the notes.log/
  9. RecordThis page, rebuilt from the notes, the screenshots and git.tools/docs/build_docs.py

Tools

HTML, CSS, JavaScriptThe whole game is index.html, with no libraries and no build step.
Canvas 2DThe 1024 by 1024 drawing pad, undo by repainting strokes, and the tall saved chain image.
Web Audio APIEvery sound effect is generated in code, so there are no audio files.
Browser APIsvisualViewport keeps the phone keyboard off the guess box; Screen Wake Lock keeps the screen on; the share sheet saves the chain on phones.
Google FontsGochi Hand for the handwritten headings and Nunito for everything else, with fallbacks when offline.
Node and Google Chrometest/cdp.js drives headless Chrome over the DevTools Protocol with no packages; copied from auxetic-chess.
Python http.servertest/run.sh serves the game on port 8766 while the test plays it.
git and GitHub PagesPublic repository juslangit/scribble-relay, published from main at juslangit.github.io/scribble-relay.

01-idea.md · 7 sections

Idea

Problem

Party and classroom games usually need a box, a pile of phones joining an online room, or an app install. Luqman wanted something that runs from one HTML file.

Proposed solution

Drawing telephone on one shared device. Players pass it around: write a phrase, draw it, guess the drawing, draw the guess. Nobody sees more than the previous turn. The reveal plays the whole chain back for the room, which is where the laughs are. Crown the funniest turn and save the chain as an image.

06-decisions.md · 4 sections

Decisions

D-001 — Pass one device around instead of phones joining a room
  • Date: 2026-09-13
  • Status: active
  • Context: Luqman asked for a party game that runs from an HTML file.
  • Options considered:
OptionProsCons
Pass-the-deviceOne file, no server, works offline, no joining codesOne person plays at a time
Each phone joins a room (Gartic Phone style)Everyone plays at onceNeeds a server or WebRTC signalling — not one file
  • Decision: Pass-the-device, one chain per game.
  • Reason: It is the only format that honours "one HTML file", and the shared reveal is the best part either way.
  • Consequences / trade-offs: A game takes roughly players × timer. "Everyone twice" exists for small groups.
  • Reversible? with difficulty
D-002 — Public repo, hosted on GitHub Pages
  • Date: 2026-09-13
  • Status: active
  • Context: Luqman wanted to try it on phone, tablet and PC. GitHub Pages on a private repo needs a paid plan.
  • Decision: Public repo juslangit/scribble-relay, Pages from main.
  • Reason: Gives one URL that opens on any device, and a party game has nothing secret in it. Matches print-quote and pipeline, which are also public.
  • Consequences / trade-offs: Code is visible to anyone. Can be made private later, which turns Pages off.
  • Reversible? easily
D-003 — Fixed 1024×1024 square canvas
  • Date: 2026-09-13
  • Status: active
  • Context: The same drawing must look right on a phone in portrait, a phone in landscape, and a projector.
  • Decision: Every drawing is a 1024×1024 square; the screen shows it scaled to the biggest square that fits.
  • Reason: A square fits both orientations without cropping, and a fixed size means a drawing made on a phone is identical on the big screen.
  • Reversible? with difficulty (older saved chains aren't stored anyway)
D-004 — Phaser as an effects layer over the page, not a rewrite
  • Date: 2026-09-18
  • Status: active (merged into main 2026-09-18, 12c62e2)
  • Context: Luqman asked for all his web games to be rebuilt on Phaser so they "look, feel and be better at everything". This game is drawing with a finger and typing guesses — the two things Phaser is worst at: its input pipeline adds lag to freehand drawing and it has no text input.
  • Options considered: (A) rewrite on Phaser (B) keep as is (C) keep the HTML game and add Phaser on top for the moments.
  • Decision: C. fx.js draws on a see-through, full-screen canvas with pointer-events: none. Its game loop sleeps and the canvas is hidden whenever nothing is playing.
  • Reason: Gets the juice and real sound without costing drawing latency or the 120 existing checks. Recommended on 2026-09-17 after the auxetic-chess pilot; Luqman said "proceed" on 2026-09-18.
  • Consequences / trade-offs: The "one file, zero dependencies" identity is gone: Phaser (1.4 MB) is vendored in vendor/, so there is still no build step and no network. If Phaser fails to load, the game falls back to its original beeps.
  • Reversible? easily — delete three script tags

04-methods.md · 4 sections

Methods

Run and test
cd ~/Desktop/project/game/scribble-relay
open index.html            # play locally
./test/run.sh              # full game in headless Chrome at 4 sizes, screenshots in test/shots/

Publishing: git push on main → GitHub Pages rebuilds https://juslangit.github.io/scribble-relay/ within a minute.

How the game is built (plain-language map of index.html)
  • Screens are <section class="screen"> blocks; show(id) hides all but one.
  • The chain is game.chain, a list of {kind, player, value, late}. Turn 0 is write, odd turns draw, even turns guess. A player sees only chain[turn-1].
  • Drawing pad: every stroke is stored as a list of points on a fixed 1024×1024 canvas, whatever the screen size. Finished strokes are painted once onto a hidden canvas; only the stroke in progress is redrawn each frame. Undo = drop the last stroke and repaint. "Clear" is stored as a step so it can be undone too.
  • Fitting to the screen: fitSquare() makes the canvas/image the largest square that fits; a ResizeObserver reruns it on rotate or keyboard open.
  • Phone keyboard: screens are sized from visualViewport, so the keyboard shrinks the drawing instead of covering the guess box.
  • Sound is generated with the Web Audio API (no files). Screen wake lock keeps phones awake during a game.
  • Saved image: buildChainImage() draws the chain onto one tall canvas. On touch devices it opens the share sheet; on desktop it downloads a PNG.
Testing pattern

test/cdp.js is a zero-dependency Chrome DevTools Protocol driver copied from auxetic-chess (port changed to 9341). test/e2e.js uses Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride + Input.dispatchTouchEvent to draw with real touch input on phone/tablet sizes and mouse events on desktop.

The project record: docs/index.html (2026-09-15)

One HTML file holds the whole record of the game — overview, pipeline, captioned screenshots, idea, planning, milestones, decisions, methods, session logs, test files and git history — in the repo and on the documentation website. Luqman's standing rule: whenever the game changes, rebuild it and republish, the same as Referee For Fun.

python3 tools/docs/build_docs.py --publish

which rebuilds docs/index.html and then runs docs-site publish, putting it live at https://luqman-docs.netlify.app/scribble-relay/ — the same link every time. These notes are read directly, so writing the knowledge base is most of updating the record. New screenshots need an entry in GALLERIES at the top of the script; a missing file shows as a labelled gap, not an error. Everything below the script's "engine" line is identical in all four game copies (auxetic-chess, bluff-show, kedai-runtuh, scribble-relay) — change it in all of them at once.

Session log

2026-09-18

What was done

  • Luqman played the Phaser version of auxetic-chess, said it was good, and asked to carry on with the other web games.
  • Added a Phaser effects layer on branch feat/phaser-fx (D-004), not merged. fx.js is a see-through Phaser canvas over the page. The game's screens, text boxes and drawing pad are untouched.
  • Moments: confetti when the chain is complete and when the reveal ends; stars in the next player's own colour on the hand-over screen; a red flash and a shake when time runs out; a ring on each of the last five seconds; a pop and a puff of sparks as each card turns over; gold stars on the crown.
  • Real sounds from Kenney's CC0 packs (sounds.js, tools/build_sounds.py), with the oscillator beeps kept as the fallback.
  • New test/fx.js: 58 checks, run twice — with Phaser's Canvas renderer and with WebGL. It checks the layer never blocks a tap, never wakes while someone draws, goes back to sleep after every effect, honours reduce-motion, and that the game plays with Phaser blocked. The 120 game checks are unchanged and pass.

Decisions made

  • D-004 — Phaser as an effects layer over the page, not a rewrite.

Stuck on / problems

  • The first confetti was white. Phaser's Canvas renderer (what a browser without WebGL gets) ignores colour tinting, and white confetti on the cream page looked like the text was being rubbed out. Colours are now painted into the textures, which works in both renderers.
  • Additive-blend sparks disappear on a light page — they glow on dark and wash out on cream. Switched to normal blending.
  • Jingles chosen without hearing them. Measured each jingle's melody instead: the good ones climb 9–10 semitones, the time's-up one falls 9. Luqman should still listen and say if any are wrong — the picks are one line each in tools/build_sounds.py.
  • Converted the sounds to MP3, because older iPhones cannot play .ogg.
  • The stock python3 -m http.server resets connections when Chrome asks for several files at once; the tests now use test/serve.py.

Next

  • to do Luqman plays feat/phaser-fx, then merge into main (that publishes it)
  • to do M2: a real party

Later the same day

  • Luqman: "proceed". feat/phaser-fx merged into main as 12c62e2, all 236 checks green on main, pushed; GitHub Pages built it, and the live page was driven in Chrome — effects layer ready on WebGL, 8 sounds decoded, confetti flying, no errors.
  • Portfolio card updated: "Zero dependencies" and "one HTML file with no libraries" were no longer true; it now says what the Phaser layer does and that it never blocks a tap.

What proves it works, from each file's own header comment

Tests and tools

Browser test

The end-to-end test that plays a whole game at four screen sizes and takes every screenshot on this page. Run it with ./test/run.sh; it needs Node and Google Chrome.

FileWhat it does
test/run.shServe the game locally and play it through headless Chrome.
test/cdp.jsMinimal Chrome DevTools Protocol driver. No dependencies.
test/e2e.jsPlays a whole game through the real UI at phone, tablet and desktop sizes, drawing with real pointer input, and screenshots every screen.
test/fx.jsThe effects layer (fx.js), checked in headless Chrome. What matters about it is mostly what it must NOT do: take a tap, cost anything while someone draws, or break the game if Phaser is missing. So most of these checks are about that, and the rest confirm the effects and sounds actually happen.
